title: Cambodia Supreme Court upholds treason convictions of 2 journalists, raising press freedom questions
content: Cambodia’s Supreme Court on Friday upheld the treason convictions and 14-year prison sentences of journalists Phorn Sopheap and Pheap Pheara, according to local media. The court rejected the journalists’ final appeal in a case that rights organizations and press groups have claimed is criminalizing reporting. The defense previously asked the court to either dismiss the case or reduce it to merely disclosing “national defense secrets.” Additionally, they requested the court to suspend the sentences pending a ruling. The ruling leaves only a royal pardon as a possible route to their release. The court delivered the decision after a brief hearing in Phnom Penh. Deputy Supreme Court Chief Taing Sunlay said that the bench had decided to uphold the appellate ruling. The Siem Reap Provincial Court had convicted the pair on December 17, 2025, in a one-day trial. Subsequently, the Court of Appeal in Battambang upheld that verdict on March 26, 2026. Under Cambodia’s Criminal Code, supplying a foreign state with information prejudicial to national defense yields seven to 15 years in prison. Their conviction and sentence had remained private until the journalists filed an appeal in February 2026. Sopheap, 39, reported for Battambang Post TV Online, and Pheara, 41, reported for TSP 68 TV Online. The two were arrested separately on July 31, 2025, as they returned from a reporting trip in Oddar Meanchey province, along the contested border with Thailand. Deadly clashes broke out beforehand, part of a wider sweep of detentions targeting journalists, activists, and opposition figures over border-related social media posts. Prosecutors alleged that their Facebook posts disclosed Cambodian military positions. One image allegedly showed both men with Cambodian soldiers at Ta Krabei Temple (Ta Kwai in Thailand). Most people haven't noticed yet.

They still open Claude, ask one question, and close the tab — treating a full operating system for work like it's a search bar.

→ LEVEL 1 — EXPLORER
You talk, it thinks.
Ask anything, pull live info, upload your docs, sharpen your writing.
Most people live here forever. This is the shallow end.

→ LEVEL 2 — BUILDER
Now it remembers.
Projects hold your files, context, and goals. Artifacts turn conversations into real docs, code, and tools you reuse.
You stop starting from zero every time.

→ LEVEL 3 — AUTOMATOR
This is where it stops feeling like a chat.
You delegate. It runs workflows, connects your apps, and keeps working while you're gone.
You're not prompting anymore. You're managing.

→ LEVEL 4 — CREATOR
It designs.
Visuals, mockups, on-brand graphics — generated, refined, exported for any platform.
The "I'll hire someone for that" tasks quietly disappear.

→ LEVEL 5 — MASTERY
It ships.
Writes, debugs, and optimizes code. Builds full apps. Runs the terminal. Connects databases, APIs, deploys.
An entire engineering loop in one place.

The pattern is the whole point:

Level 1 you ask.
Level 5 it executes.

Everyone's fighting over better prompts at Level 1.
The real leverage was three levels up the whole time.

Which level are you actually using? 👇

content:
OpenAI just launched a model nobody can use, to beat a competitor the government already banned.

Sol tops Claude Mythos on coding benchmarks — but Mythos is offline because Washington pulled it two weeks ago, and Sol is locked to ~20 approved companies for the same reason.

Think about how strange that is. The two best AI labs in the world are now competing on charts for models the public can't touch. The race isn't "who builds the smartest model" anymore. It's "who the U.S. government clears for launch first."

Capability used to be the moat. Then speed. Now it's clearance. Every frontier model in America ships on Washington's schedule, or it doesn't ship.

Move fast and break things is officially dead. Welcome to ask permission and wait.
